title: Eating und nutritional habits in athletes and controls - a longitudinal examination
summary: In elite sports, sport-specific eating, nutritional, and training habits can help athletes to reach their full athletic potential. At the same time, elite sports can represent an increased risk for the development of disordered eating. The ENHANCE-study investigates which indicators can point to disordered eating in elite athletes practicing ballet, bodybuilding, racket sports, soccer and basketball compared to the general population (control group). In the long term, we want to determine the protective and risk mechanisms that influence eating habits in elite sports. The study design is a longitudinal cohort study with follow-up assessments at one, six and twelve months after the baseline assessment.

interventions.name: Investigational group: n = 312 elite athletes from weight-sensitive (ballet and bodybuilding) and less weight-sensitive (racket sports, soccer and basketball) sports will be assessed four times (T0-T3) in online-surveys about their eating and training behavior. In addition, n = 90 clinical interview

Control group: n = 312 participants from the general population who do not meet the criteria of an elite athlete will be assessed four times (T0-T3) about their eating behavior. Diagnostic interviews and body measurements are not carried out on the control group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All participants should fluently speak and understand English. This study specifies on elite athletes either practicing ballet, bodybuilding, or ballgames (tennis, soccer, basketball) on a professional level, which is defined as organising their daily life around their sport or regular participation at competitions or performances. The training should have been practiced for at least 6 months with more than 300 min/week with at least moderate intensity to be considered an elite athlete.  If participants meet the criteria to be considered an elite athlete and they practice one of the sports disciplines, participation in the study is possible in the Elite Athlete Group. The specification on some sport-disciplines enables sufficient large samples per sport disciplines to investigate differences between the sport disciplines.
Participants are assigned to the Control Group, if they do not meet the criteria of the Elite Athletes Group. Participants from the Control Group can also exercise regularly, but with lower training load, intensity and professionalism.
Exclusion criteria:
If participants meet the criteria to be considered an elite athlete but they do not practice one of the sport-disciplines, study participation is not possible.
